title: Market Pulse
body_html:
This post reflects my current views on the market, sectors, and internal breadth/momentum. Expect candid, data-driven analysis, peppered with personal insights drawn from years of trading experience. I aim to provide value in every edition, helping you to see the market through a clearer, more informed lens.

What You Can Expect

  • In-Depth Market Analysis: A thorough examination of market trends, key indices, and pivotal turning points.

  • Sector Spotlights: A closer look at the hottest (and not-so-hot) sectors, highlighting opportunities and risks.

  • Breadth and Momentum Insights: Understanding the underlying strength of the market through breadth indicators and momentum metrics.

  • Themes and Setups: A look at the top stock in terms of relative strength, momentum, trend, volatility, and liquidity to spot themes, setups, and opportunities

Exclusive Features

  • Interactive Spreadsheet: Alongside each post, I’ll be linking a detailed spreadsheet that tracks the breadth and momentum metrics. This will allow you to follow along with the data and see the trends I’m analyzing day-by-day.

  • Quick Video Commentary: To complement the metrics, I’ll also be posting a quick video commentary several days a week

    . This will provide a more dynamic overview of the market, offering you additional context and clarity.

Market Metrics

Overall: Positive

The major indices continue to demonstrate constructive price and trend behavior, with a consistent pattern of higher highs and higher lows firmly supported by rising 10- and 20-day moving averages. Notably, the 50-day moving averages are beginning to turn upward as well, thanks to sustained strength in recent sessions—further validating the underlying uptrend. As long as this structure holds, there are no immediate technical red flags.

Market internals also remain supportive. The breadth of new highs versus new lows remains firmly positive, indicating that a broad base of individual stocks are participating in the advance. Additionally, up-versus-down momentum metrics continue to favor buyers, suggesting that the average stock is expanding upward rather than contracting—an encouraging sign for continued market strength.

From a sector perspective, leadership has rotated decisively toward risk-on areas. Technology, consumer discretionary, financials, and industrials are leading the relative strength rankings, while previous defensive leaders—such as utilities and consumer staples—are losing ground and starting to roll over. This shift in leadership suggests a rotation of institutional capital into growth-oriented sectors, a bullish signal for the market’s intermediate-term health.

Risk Management and Exposure Control

Maintain a Constructively Bullish Stance:
The market continues to hold a healthy uptrend, with major indices maintaining levels above rising 10-, 20-, and now upward-sloping 50-day moving averages. Given this strength, a bullish posture is warranted, but proceed with caution as markets approach potential resistance and extended names begin to digest recent gains.

Scale Exposure Responsibly:
Continue adding exposure selectively, focusing on fresh, high-quality setups emerging from consolidation. Avoid chasing extended names. Prioritize clean entries with favorable reward-to-risk profiles.

Manage Lagging Positions Proactively:
Reduce or close positions that are lagging the broader move, losing relative strength, or failing at resistance. Rotate capital into names that are holding trend and showing signs of continued leadership.

Market Monitoring and Internal Indicators

Monitor Price Structure and Trend Continuity:
The uptrend remains intact, supported by consistent higher lows and improving slope across key moving averages. Keep an eye on how small caps handle their recent 50-day breakout and whether large/mid caps maintain higher support zones during any pullbacks.

Track Internal Breadth and Momentum:
While internals remain positive, the strong skew seen in recent weeks has eased closer to neutral. This suggests a maturing move that could lead to short-term consolidation. A pause here would be healthy if internals remain stable and setups continue to build.

Watch for Divergences and Warning Signs:
Any deterioration in internals—especially if not confirmed by price action—should be treated as an early warning. Monitor leadership for weakening RS lines, shrinking breakout success, or narrowing sector participation.

Sector and Theme Development

Confirm Rotation into Growth-Oriented Sectors:
Tech, Financials, Consumer, and Industrials are leading the RS rankings. Watch for continuation in these areas, particularly tech, which has rebounded after a brief drop in strength.

Avoid Defensive Laggards:
Utilities and Staples continue to fall down the sector rankings, suggesting institutional appetite for offense over defense. Energy and Healthcare are rolling over near resistance—manage exposure cautiously in these areas.

Identify Emerging Strength:
Scan for early basing activity and RS improvement in under-the-radar groups. These may become the next leadership clusters as the market rotates.

Capital Allocation and Trade Execution

Focus on Setup Quality, Not Quantity:
Target stocks with:

  • Breakouts from proper bases with volume

  • Pullbacks to rising moving averages that hold

  • Clear relative strength against sector peers and the market

Tighten Risk Parameters:
Set clear stops below logical support zones. Avoid oversized exposure to any single name or sector, particularly those showing late-stage behavior or resistance rejections.

Keep Some Cash Available:
Maintain flexibility. With sector rotation and digestion likely, having dry powder allows you to act decisively as new leadership emerges.

Daily Reassessment and Strategy Adaptation

Expect Retests of Key Support:
Retests of rising 10-/20-day moving averages are likely and healthy. Confirm that support holds on pullbacks—failure could signal deeper correction or stall.

Adjust Exposure Dynamically:

  • If internals and sector participation expand: Increase exposure gradually into breakout-quality setups.

  • If setups begin to fail or breadth narrows: Step back, reduce exposure, and preserve gains.

Let Setups Lead the Way:
Ignore headline noise and day-to-day index fluctuations. Let the number and quality of technical setups determine your level of engagement.

Key Focus Areas

  • Patience on Entry: Don’t chase breakouts. Wait for orderly pullbacks or volume-backed bases.

  • Watch Leadership Transitions: Confirm that tech, consumer, financials, and industrials continue to lead or make room for new sectors to rotate in.

  • Stay Flexible and Reactive: This is still a fluid market. Quickly trim exposure if deterioration arises and be ready to re-engage if setups reassert.

Bottom Line

The trend remains positive, supported by solid technical structure and constructive internal readings. However, momentum is moderating, and the market may be entering a digestion phase. Stay constructively bullish, but remain selective. Allow pullbacks to set up new opportunities, manage risk tightly, and let high-quality setups—not hope—guide your exposure.
